tagline: An international educational services company focused on providing quality learning experiences that cultivate and enhance students' creativity
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the primary revenue driver for the company, representing nearly 70% of total revenues. Although the sector is technology, AACG operates in creative education, where this segment is the most strategic.

kpis.name: Portfolio Training Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from project-based or time-based training programs.
kpis.description: Accounted for 69.8% of revenue in 2025. Decline due to increased competition and pricing adjustments.
kpis.signal: Key revenue stream declining despite overall stability

kpis.name: Other Educational Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from services such as overseas study consulting and research-based learning.
kpis.description: Growth driven by art classes in partner schools and value-added services.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting direct costs.
kpis.description: Decline linked to rising costs of outsourced services and part-time instructors.
kpis.signal: Margin compression due to external costs

kpis.name: Net Loss
kpis.explanation: Amount lost over the year after all expenses.
kpis.description: Net loss of $6.9 million in 2025 compared to $5.2 million in 2024.

kpis.name: R&D Expenses
kpis.explanation: Money spent to develop new educational programs.
kpis.description: R&D expenses estimated at approximately $0.5 million for the year.

kpis.name: Student Enrollment
kpis.explanation: Total number of students enrolled in the last quarter.
kpis.description: 921 students in Q4 2025 versus 1,038 a year earlier.

kpis.name: Credit Hours
kpis.explanation: Total number of training hours delivered.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue sourced from SEC EDGAR company facts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).

risks.title: Uncertain regulation of private schools
risks.score_rationale: Central position in the 10-K, strong language ("materially and negatively affect"), increasing trend due to recent regulatory changes, high weight as it relates to the very existence of training centers.

risks.title: VIE structure exposed to regulatory risk
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the first section of risks, alarming language ("value of our ADS could become zero"), stable but critical trend, maximum weight as it is the group's core structure.

risks.title: Lack of ICP license for online services
risks.score_rationale: Secondary but explicit position, concerning language ("suspension of operations"), increasing trend with the rise of digital services, high importance as it relates to growing digitalization.

risks.title: Lack of travel agency license
risks.score_rationale: Present in the licenses section, clear language on risks ("illegal revenues confiscated"), stable trend, moderate to high weight as it relates to a secondary but strategic activity.

risks.title: Cross-border cybersecurity control risk
risks.score_rationale: Identified as a mandatory future risk, severe language ("suspension of operations, site closures"), increasing trend with growing Chinese regulation, high weight.

risks.title: Dependence on acquisition of key talent
risks.score_rationale: Not explicitly mentioned but implied in the educational model, moderate language, stable trend, moderate weight as it relates to teaching quality.

risks.title: Competition in the art education market
risks.score_rationale: Implicit but strong presence in market discussion, assertive language on leadership position, increasing trend, high weight as a direct threat to market share.

risks.title: Evolution of personal data policies
risks.score_rationale: Present in future risks, strict language ("suspension of operations, license revocation"), increasing trend, high weight due to sensitivity of student data.

ai_positioning.summary: AACG does not mention any strategy or use of artificial intelligence in its educational services or operations. Initiatives focus on academic partnerships and in-person or hybrid programs.
evidence: No mention of AI in services or products
No reference to automated learning tools or generative AI
Focus on human-led Master Classes and in-person workshops
